author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Stays inside the vet feature package (system-design § Package Structure; ADR feature-package-organization) and server-rendered Thymeleaf (ADR server-side-rendering-with-thymeleaf); no new module, dependency, or pattern. Adjustment: three new types, each an In-force catalog pattern (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog). SpecialtyRepository is a lookup repository mirroring PetTypeRepository's name-ordered read, needed because a specialty nobody holds (edge case 2) cannot be derived from veterinarians. SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable value object that owns every directory rule: all specialties listed, a veterinarian under each specialty held, a veterinarian with none omitted, first-then-last full name, stable order. It keeps those rules out of the controller (Design Principle 4; catalog Web controller row). SpecialtyController is a thin entry point: load both collections, build the directory, render. Design-doc writes: REQ-VET-003 joined to Contracts rows Vet, Specialty, VetRepository; new rows SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyController; one Invariants sentence; a new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-directory row. Basis for existing symbols is grep/read, not the IDE oracle (not connected): VetRepository.findAll() cached collection, Vet.getSpecialties(), PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes() @Query ORDER BY name, layout fragment layout(template, menu).
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html on SpecialtyController, package-private like VetController. Binding target: none; the handler binds no request parameter and no form object, and stray query parameters are ignored. No persisted type is bound (security-principles § Trust Boundaries).

SpecialtyRepository extends Spring Data's Repository<Specialty, Integer> (the narrow marker VetRepository uses, not JpaRepository) with one read-only method returning every specialty ordered by name. It is uncached; the vets cache on VetRepository is reused unchanged via findAll().

SpecialtyDirectory is built by a static factory from the specialty collection and the veterinarian collection. It holds an immutable list of entries, each carrying the specialty's stored name and an immutable list of veterinarian full names. It keeps no Vet or Specialty reference, so it realizes the closed Domain Core properties in full; the persistence-entity exception does not extend to it.

Template renders through fragments/layout with a menu value matching no nav item, so no nav entry highlights and none is added (PRD non-goal: no entry point). Specialty and veterinarian names render via th:text (escaped), never translated. Any new user-facing wording is a message key present in messages.properties and all eleven locale bundles (REQ-LANG-002, enforced by I18nPropertiesSyncTest); the existing 'specialties' key may be reused.

Double for the repository boundary in controller tests: hand-written in-memory implementations of VetRepository and SpecialtyRepository, registered via a @TestConfiguration in @WebMvcTest(SpecialtyController.class). Both interfaces are narrow Repository-marker interfaces, so a hand-written double fits and no Mockito stub is sanctioned (testing-principles § Mocking Policy). The more-specialties-than-one-vet-page case supplies six or more specialties through the double.
Double for the framework transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned web-layer harness (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy).

SpecialtyDirectory rules (every specialty, several-specialty veterinarian under each, no-specialty veterinarian omitted, unheld specialty listed empty, full-name form, stable order) are unit-tested with real Vet and Specialty objects and no doubles.

patterns.description: name-ordered read of a lookup entity via @Query ORDER BY name
constructor-injected repository, @GetMapping *.html returning a vets/ view name
layout fragment use, firstName + ' ' + lastName full-name rendering, table markup

risks.risk: The specialty-directory path reads every specialty and every veterinarian per request (system-design § Scale and Load, specialty-directory row).
risks.mitigation: Simplest readable form: two full reads and one in-memory grouping pass; no paging, query projection, or custom cache. The row records the size as unrecorded and treated as bounded.

risks.risk: Grouping, omission, or ordering logic drifting into SpecialtyController as a new controller-held rule (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row; Design Principle 4).
risks.mitigation: All directory rules live in SpecialtyDirectory. The controller only loads, delegates to the factory, and adds the result to the model.

risks.risk: Unstable ordering from HashSet-backed Vet.specialties or unordered findAll() (PRD REQ-VET-003 edge case 3).
risks.mitigation: Specialties come name-ordered from the repository. SpecialtyDirectory sorts the veterinarians within each specialty deterministically, by last name, then first name, then id. The PRD requires no particular sort.

risks.risk: An untranslated literal in the new template breaks REQ-LANG-002 (security-principles n/a; system-design § Contracts note on REQ-LANG-002).
risks.mitigation: All static wording goes through #{...} keys present in every bundle; I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails the build otherwise.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records to audit. No ADR: the value-object placement and new repository instantiate In-force catalog patterns and constrain no later slice beyond what the brief already states. The § Scale and Load section did not exist in docs/system-design.md; this dispatch creates it with the one row this slice needs. The new sibling controller follows the naming rule's 'domain noun' prefix; folding the route into VetController would equally conform, and SpecialtyController is the recorded choice.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository.java adds a single static JPQL query ('@Query("SELECT specialty FROM Specialty specialty ORDER BY specialty.name")') with no parameters and no request-derived text; VetRepository is reused unchanged.

Cross-site scripting: specialtyList.html renders specialtyName and veterinarian names only through th:text (escaped). 'grep -F -e th:utext -r src/main/resources/templates' returned no hits. The template adds no inline script, no remote resource and no request-derived href.

Template-expression evaluation: the only preprocessing in the path is the pre-existing layout.html:31 'th:href="@{__${link}__}"'. It receives fixed literal links from the layout's own menuItem calls, and the new template passes only the literal menu name 'specialties' into the layout fragment. No request text reaches expression evaluation.

Mass assignment and input validation: SpecialtyController.showSpecialtyDirectory is a parameterless @GetMapping("/specialties.html") that binds no @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody and reads no request parameter, so there is no boundary input to validate and no binder allow-list is needed.

Exposed surface: the change adds one read-only, idempotent GET route that shows specialty names and vet full names. These are the same data the existing /vets.html already publishes, so it grows the open-route baseline in docs/security-principles.md by no new data class and mutates nothing. build.gradle and application*.properties are unchanged (git status --porcelain showed nothing for them), so management exposure is unchanged.

Resource use: the directory reads all specialties plus the @Cacheable("vets") VetRepository.findAll(). docs/system-design.md § Scale and Load records this as bounded. No web route creates specialties or vets (no such route was found in this review), so an attacker cannot grow the working set.
Error and secret handling: the new code throws no exception, adds no logging and holds no credentials; the diff contains no token/password/secret/key literal.
Concurrency: SpecialtyController holds only final repository references. SpecialtyDirectory is built per request and immutable (List.copyOf in the constructor and in the Entry record).

Supply chain: no dependency change in this diff. OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze is not configured in build.gradle (grep -F 'dependencyCheck' found nothing), so no NVD match ran. Resolved runtime versions from './gradlew dependencies': spring-webmvc 7.0.9, tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind 3.1.5, thymeleaf-spring6 3.1.5.RELEASE, on Spring Boot 4.1.0 per CLAUDE.md.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: No test runs the new stack against a real datastore. The controller tests use hand-written in-memory repositories, and the directory tests use constructed entities. `grep -F -e "specialties.html" -e "SpecialtyRepository" src/test`, excluding the two new vet/Specialty* files, returns nothing, so PetClinicIntegrationTests and the DB-backed tests never reach the route or the repository. Nothing exercises the path the PRD bullet 'given the clinic's specialties' describes: the seeded specialties and veterinarians read through JPA, including the cached `VetRepository.findAll()` with its eagerly fetched specialties. A broken mapping or fetch would pass every current test. A specialty held by nobody is the case the query's Javadoc promises, and it is also unread from real data. Change it would catch: a mapping, fetch or cache regression that leaves `SpecialtyDirectory.of` and the template correct.
findings.fix: Add one real-stack test: either a `@SpringBootTest`/`@AutoConfigureMockMvc` case in the style of PetClinicIntegrationTests that GETs `/specialties.html` against the seed data (three specialties, six veterinarians) and asserts a seeded specialty with its veterinarian full name is rendered, or a `@DataJpaTest` on `SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties()`. One test is enough; do not repeat the ordering table.

findings.description: Same equivalence class as theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithTheVeterinariansHoldingIt in the same file. It uses the same inputs (RADIOLOGY, HELEN_LEARY) and its assertion, Entry("radiology", List.of("Helen Leary")), is already contained in the first test's containsExactly. No change that fails this test would pass the first, so it costs reading time and catches nothing extra.
findings.fix: Delete it and let the first test carry Done-when bullet 2, or give it the distinguishing input (a first name sorting after the last name) so it fails where the first does not.

findings.description: `createASpecialty` and `createAVet` are defined twice in the two new test files with the same bodies (the controller version takes one specialty, the directory version varargs). The brief's § Test Data Construction and Testing Vocabulary ask for one shared vocabulary reused before new helpers are added. Two copies mean a Vet or Specialty constructor change is fixed twice.
findings.fix: Keep the varargs `createAVet` and `createASpecialty` in one package-private test helper in the vet test package (or reuse an existing one) and call it from both suites.

recommendations: SpecialtyControllerTests.theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyWithTheVeterinariansHoldingIt builds its expected model attribute by calling production SpecialtyDirectory.of, which re-runs another unit's logic. The two content assertions already pin the boundary behavior. Consider dropping the model-attribute line so the controller suite stays at the boundary (non-blocking).

The directory-level test theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldShowASpecialtyNameAsStored passes the name straight through and would fail only if someone added a transform. The rendered-page assertion in the controller suite is what guards edge case 4. It is acceptable as is.
approved_aspects: Verified by reading the tests and running `./gradlew test --tests '*vet.Specialty*'`: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, all 6 declared tests present per `grading.py coverage-map --feature REQ-VET-003`.

Placement follows system-design: the grouping and ordering rules live in SpecialtyDirectory, a value object assigned below the boundary, and are tested there with real entities and no doubles. The controller suite keeps two boundary paths (view and content, and the unpaged single page).
Mocking policy honored: no Mockito; the in-memory repositories are hand-written and MockMvc is the sanctioned harness.

Edge cases 1 (several specialties), 2 (unheld specialty) and 3 (stable order by specialty name, then last and first name of the veterinarians) each have a dedicated unit test, and all four Done-when bullets have a named test.

Naming follows the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school; AssertJ fluent assertions with containsExactly and whole-Entry comparison; four-phase structure with no phase comments; no branching in test bodies.
